trajectory_summary: The call opens on a cooperative inbound callback, dips into real friction when the rep runs a legitimate but customer-facing hold protocol, then recovers fully and rides an unusually long personal/political/commercial-real-estate tangent without losing the booking. The rep closed the mechanical needs (bill photo, usage graph, appointment slot) despite the tangents, landing a booked appointment with a specific time.
outcome_dispute: None on the outcome itself — a specific day and time (tomorrow, 02:30) were confirmed at 17:38, so 'booked' via phone channel is the correct tag. Note there is no evidence of a co-owner/spouse on this account; customer stated she is sole owner of the building.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (02:30) were explicitly confirmed by the customer, and the rep restated it at close: "let's plan on 02:30 tomorrow, Emery." No co-owner was identified — customer stated she is sole owner of the building — so co_owner_confirmed is not applicable.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the stated bill amount and logged it but never flipped it into an emotional alignment-against-the-utility line (e.g., framing the $181.80 as money currently going to ComEd that could instead build equity). The conversation moved straight into the incentive/ownership Q&A instead.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Framing qualification checks to avoid triggering scam suspicion
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I do want to just double check with my manager and make sure we are able to help.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This single line produced the sharpest friction of the call — the customer directly challenged the rep's logic and nearly derailed rapport. The underlying check was legitimate, but opening with doubt language on an owner-occupied multi-unit building (an edge case that's usually fine) reads as a stall. Reframe to lead with the likely-positive read before floating disqualification language.

key_moments.quote: I do want to just double check with my manager and make sure we are able to help.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep did not know how to resolve a tenant-paid-meter edge case and admitted it via a manager check rather than guessing or fabricating an answer — the admit-and-recover path, not a fabrication. The customer's hostile reaction was to the WAY it was delivered (framed as a possible disqualifier) more than the check itself.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Right. I'm just a a scheduler, so I don't really know a bunch of the specifics. Right?
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the correct scope-holding line, but it arrived on the FOURTH attempt at the same ownership/cost question, after three earlier answers (bill swap explanation, ownership vs. leasing options, 'equipment isn't free') that each invited another round.

key_moments.quote: I got 600,000 to put solar on the resort right now. So I'm trying to figure out what's gonna be my best plan.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer disclosed a large-scale commercial/international solar buying intent (resort in Belize, apartment portfolio, $600K budget) that is entirely outside Ion's residential single-family/multi-unit script. The schema has no defined signal or routing path for B2B/commercial disclosures — this is a genuine schema gap, not a rep execution failure.
